newsitem.title: UK: Labour slams UK government's economic performance.
newsitem.headline: Labour slams UK government's economic performance.

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair on Tuesday criticised Conservative claims that the British economy was booming, saying the country had fallen behind other industrial nations during 18 years of Conservative rule.

"(Prime Minister John) Major talks as if Britain was booming and the rest of Europe collapsing in rubble. Fact; Germans earn 15 percent more than we do. Fact: The French ecnomy with a population about the same as ours is 20 percent bigger than ours. Fact; Italy is ahead of us in the economic league," Blair told a news conference.

Blair said the reasons for Britain falling behind were straight forward. The ruling Conservatives, he said, had failed to deliver a "strong stable economy." Britain had suffered the two worst recessions since World war Two in the period after the Conservatives took power in 1979.
Blair said companies had not had the confidence to invest in their businesses, peoples' skills had not been developed and the needs and interests of small businesses had been ignored.

"Too little stabilty, not enough investment in business and in skills. A failure to back small businesses and entrepreneurs. Britain deserves better. This time we need a recovery which doesn't end in tears," he said.
Blair repeated the pledges he has made for a Labour government which he said would provide the foundations for sustained growth.

He said a Labour government would set a target of 2.5 percent or less for inflation, maintain a firm grip on public spending, work within spending ceilings set by the current government and keep public debt within stable and prudent levels.
